subject: chemistry

resources.title: Chemistry 2e
resources.notes: Two-semester general chemistry scope; use foundation mapping only for its introductory/review material, not for the entire text.

resources.title: Principles of Chemical Science
resources.notes: Freshman-level independent-study chemistry. Covers atomic/molecular electronic structure, bonding, thermodynamics, equilibrium, redox, transition metals, kinetics and catalysis; high-school review material supports only introductory cells.

resources.title: Principles of Chemical Science
resources.notes: More mathematically demanding introductory chemistry for students with a strong chemistry background; not mapped downward to foundation/beginner.

resources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare Chemistry Collection
resources.notes: Discovery collection only; individual courses must be verified before exact-cell ingestion.

resources.title: PubChem
resources.notes: Authoritative chemical information database; database access alone does not establish learner readiness.

resources.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: Reference data layer for thermochemical, thermophysical and spectral work; not treated as a stand-alone curriculum.

resources.title: Electrochemical Energy Systems
resources.notes: Graduate course on electrochemical energy conversion and storage, including thermodynamics, kinetics, transport, electrostatics and applications to batteries, fuel cells and supercapacitors. Advanced mapping reflects prerequisite-rich specialist material and is not down-mapped to beginner levels.

resources.title: Synthesis of Polymers
resources.notes: Dedicated graduate polymer-synthesis course. Specialist coverage only; it does not establish foundation or beginner polymer-chemistry readiness.

resources.title: Polymer Science Laboratory
resources.notes: Undergraduate polymer laboratory course supporting practical polymer/materials chemistry. Laboratory-course presence does not count as verified hands-on competency until runtime/project assessment exists.

resources.title: Computational Quantum Mechanics of Molecular and Extended Systems
resources.notes: Specialist computational quantum-mechanics course for molecular and extended systems. Research mapping denotes research-relevant methods/material, not independent research competence.

resources.title: Computational Chemistry Comparison and Benchmark Database
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: NIST SRD 101 provides experimental and computed quantum-chemistry benchmark data and comparison tools. Reference evidence complements instruction but is not a stand-alone curriculum.

resources.title: Atmospheric Chemistry
resources.notes: Graduate atmospheric chemistry provides a rigorous environmental-chemistry specialization. It does not cover the entire environmental chemistry field, so broader water, soil and contaminant chemistry remain targets.

known_gaps: Dedicated foundation/beginner curricula remain thin for analytical chemistry, biochemistry, materials chemistry, electrochemistry, polymer chemistry, computational chemistry and environmental chemistry; advanced university material is not down-mapped merely to increase coverage.

Environmental chemistry coverage is currently strongest in atmospheric chemistry; dedicated authoritative water, soil, contaminant fate and environmental analytical chemistry instruction remains a target.
Graduate and research-level readiness still requires current primary literature, laboratory or computational practice, verification and assessment rather than course or database access alone.
Specialist laboratory methods and spectroscopy should only be expanded when exact taxonomy mappings and source evidence are verified.
